Reporting Scope  
and Boundary 
The Report includes both standalone and 
consolidated information of Prestige Estates 
Projects Limited. It is well defined, concise, and 
covers Company-related events and information 
predominantly from April 1, 2024, to March 31, 
2025. The Report articulates our organizational 
strategy, governance, performance and prospects, 
in the context of our external environment and 
value creation abilities for all our stakeholders. This 
has expanded the audience beyond the primary 
provider of financial capital, to other stakeholders, 
including employees, customers, brand partners, 
local communities, regulators, and policymakers. Financial and  
Non-Financial Reporting 
This report covers both our financial  
and non-financial performances, including 
environmental and social performance. It also 
details our short-, medium-and long-term value 
creation processes/strategies, opportunities, risks, 
and outcomes attributable to or associated with 
our key stakeholders, which have a significant 
influence on our ability to create value and remain 
sustainable. Approach  
to Reporting
We have significantly enhanced our reporting 
practices, and as part of our commitment to 
transparency and stakeholder engagement, we 
are pleased to present our latest Integrated Annual 
Report (IR). This report provides a comprehensive 
overview of our performance across the six capitals 
outlined in the Integrated Reporting Framework: 
Financial, Manufactured, Intellectual, Human, Social 
and Relationship, and Natural Capital.Framework,  
Guidelines and Standards 
The financial and statutory data presented in 
this Report is in line with the requirements of the 
Companies Act, 2013 (including the rules made 
thereunder); Indian Accounting Standards (Ind 
AS); the Securities and Exchange Board of India 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015; and the Secretarial Standards.

This Report is intended to address the information 
requirements of key stakeholders, including 
investors, customers, regulators, employees, and 
society at large.Management

The Foundation Holds   
The Future Calls
Real estate in India is no longer defined by 
buildings alone. It is now shaped by ambition, 
resilience and the ability to read the shifting 
rhythms of a rapidly transforming nation. In 
this evolving landscape, where cities grow, 
lifestyles transform, and aspirations rise, there 
is a heightened need for a developer who not 
only understands these changing preferences 
but anticipates them and delivers with the 
hallmark quality, timeliness, and trust that 
Prestige is known for . 
Over the decades, we have led from the front, 
setting benchmarks, shaping skylines, and 
redefining standards across the real estate 
landscape. As pioneers in several landmark 
developments, we have never stood still. We 
continue to evolve with agility and foresight, 
creating spaces that not just meet the needs of 
today but anticipate the demands of tomorrow.
Our presence today spans key markets and 
multiple verticals, from Residential and 
Commercial to Retail and Hospitality. But more 
than geography or asset class, it is the strength 
of our foundation, our people, our culture, and 
our approach that defines us. Through cycles, 
through uncertainty, through the constant 
motion of the industry, this foundation has 
held firm.Now, we find ourselves at an inflection point. 
The demand for quality real estate is rising in 
tandem with the aspirations of a new India. 
Urban centres are becoming more connected, 
infrastructure is unlocking fresh potential, and 
the digital economy is reshaping how people 
live, work and consume. These shifts bring new 
possibilities, ones that align seamlessly with 
our next chapter .
That is the promise behind this year’s theme, 
The Foundation Holds. The Future Calls. 
It speaks of the strength of what we have 
built and the clarity of what we are building 
towards. It reflects a company rooted in 
stability, yet constantly evolving. It captures 
our commitment to move forward, not just with 
ambition, but with purpose.
The years ahead are full of opportunity. And 
we are stepping into this new chapter with 
the same principles that brought us here: 
vision, integrity, and the quiet confidence of 
a business that knows both where it stands 
and where it’s going. Everything we achieved 
over the last four decades, we are poised to 
replicate, at an even greater pace, within the 
next five years. That is the scale at which we 
are operating today. The journey so far has not 
only shaped our legacy but also strengthened 
our resilience, preparing us to navigate the 
future with conviction.How to Read across the Report Report Navigation

The Legacy that Sets 
Tomorrow in Motion About the Company
Prestige Estates Projects Limited along with its subsidiaries, joint ventures and 
associates (also referred to as ‘Prestige’, ‘The Company’ or ‘We’) started out in 
1986 with a single idea: to shape spaces that people could believe in. Spaces 
that elevate everyday living, endure through time, and quietly embody quality. 
That idea grew into something much larger, a name that today stands among 
the most trusted in Indian real estate.
Over the years, we have not only built a business 
but also earned a reputation founded on trust 
and excellence. We have built a reputation across 
Residential, Commercial, Retail and Hospitality 
segments. Each project reflects a clear intent: 
to deliver quality that’s consistent, design that’s 
thoughtful, and value that lasts.
Over the past decade, our presence has expanded 
across 13 key markets in India. As we have grown, 
we have stayed true to what matters: integrity 
in execution, precision in detail, and relevance in 
everything we create. Our work carries the Prestige 
signature, not just in scale, but in the experience it 
offers.
Our journey has evolved well beyond core real 
estate, as we continue to build complementary 
capabilities that strengthen and elevate our 
overall value proposition. With Morph, our in-
house design and manufacturing studio, we infuse 
every space with creativity and craftsmanship, 
delivering bespoke interiors, custom-designed 
furniture, and precision-engineered doors that 
blend functionality with aesthetic finesse. K2K 
Infra, our dedicated contracting arm, empowers 
us to execute construction seamlessly in-house. 
This gives us greater agility, tighter control, and the 
ability to deliver even complex or fast-track projects 
with precision and speed. Through our integrated 
property management vertical, we ensure that 
every development continues to be nurtured and 
maintained with the same attention to detail, 
aesthetic integrity, and visionary approach that 
define the Prestige experience.
Innovation fuels everything we do. It informs our 
planning, sharpens our execution, and helps us 
anticipate the evolving needs of our customers and cities. But more than innovation, it is our consistency 
that people trust. As we look ahead, we remain 
focussed on creating with purpose and building with 
clarity. The future will bring new challenges, new 
opportunities, and new ideas, and we are ready to 
lead with all the strength we have built so far .

That is why homebuyers return, investors stay, and

Relationships that Go the Distance

instrumental in delivering success, project after 
project.
Design that Does More

shaped by thoughtful design choices that prioritise 
performance, efficiency, and sustainability. Our 
developments are envisioned not just as buildings, 
but as enduring spaces that elevate lifestyles and 
create lasting value for communities.Right Place. Right Time. Real Impact.
Our projects are located in dynamic urban centres that are propelling India’s growth story. These are more 
than markets they are vibrant, evolving ecosystems shaped by industry, technology, tourism, education, and 
culture. Our presence in these cities enables us to anticipate change, respond in real time, and create spaces 
that align with how people live, work, and connect, today and in the future. Every project we undertake is a 
reflection of the city’s unique character, while also raising the bar for quality and innovation. In doing so, we 
contribute meaningfully to the transformation and progress of the communities we serve.

Dear Stakeholders,
FY 25 was a year of steady resolve and purposeful progress, as we remained anchored to the core 
principles that have long shaped our journey -  timely execution, customer-centricity, innovation-
driven development, and a proactive approach to regulatory preparedness. While certain external 
headwinds, most notably delays in key approvals, tested the tempo of our plans, they also reinforced 
the strength of our internal systems, governance discipline, and leadership. We are pleased to share 
that the year culminated on a strong note. A sharp rebound in the fourth quarter across several 
critical metrics signalled a meaningful recovery, operational stability, and a renewed readiness 
to scale. The consistency of our performance across markets and asset classes reaffirms our belief 
in the long-term potential of India’s real estate sector and Prestige’s ability to lead from the front 
within this landscape. Enduring Foundations. Expansive Horizons.Message from the Chairman and Managing Director
Capitalising on India’s Economic 
Momentum
FY 25 marked a period of moderated yet resilient 
growth for India, with GDP at a healthy 6.5%. While 
this reflected a natural tapering from the 8.2% 
in FY 24, the underlying momentum remained 
strong, supported by prudent macroeconomic 
management, continued public investment in 
infrastructure and growing consumer confidence. 
Together, these factors reaffirmed India’s position 
as a key driver of global economic growth. This 
economic momentum translated into sustained 
strength in the real estate sector, which maintained 
its upward trajectory across asset classes. India’s 
real estate sector demonstrated robust and broad-
based performance in 2024, reflecting the country’s 
resilient economic momentum. This strength 
translated into a sustained upward trajectory across 
asset classes, reinforcing long-term confidence 
in the sector .  India’s real estate sector continued 
to exhibit broad-based strength in 2024, with key 
segments demonstrating encouraging momentum. 
Residential demand remained resilient, supported 
by rising homeownership aspirations and continued 
urban development. The office market saw healthy 
absorption, underpinned by strong occupier 
confidence and expansion across technology and 
services sectors and demand from GCCs. Retail real 
estate showed steady growth, driven by domestic 
consumption and retailer optimism, while the 
hospitality sector experienced a notable revival, 
buoyed by robust domestic travel and increased 
corporate and individual spending. Together, these 
trends reflect the sector’s inherent resilience and its 
pivotal role in shaping India’s economic landscape.With policy reforms driving transparency, 
institutional confidence rising, and urbanization 
gaining higher traction, India’s real estate sector 
is entering a new phase of structural evolution.  
At Prestige, we are well-positioned to lead through 
this transformation with a focussed expansion 
strategy, prudent capital allocation, and a balanced 
presence across high-growth corridors. As we shape 
modern skylines and reimagine urban living, we 
remain committed to creating assets of enduring 
value, harnessing our extensive industry expertise, 
execution excellence, and quality centricity.

Strategic Milestones and Growth 
Highlights
Building on the macro tailwinds and sectoral 
momentum, FY 25 stood out as a pivotal year in 
Prestige’s evolution, reflecting the strength of our 
foundation and the ability to translate vision into 
tangible outcomes. In August 2024, we successfully 
concluded ₹ 5,000 Cr Qualified Institutional 
Placement (QIP), a strategic move that significantly 
strengthened our balance sheet and enhanced 
our financial flexibility to drive future growth. The 
offering witnessed demand that was multiple times 
the QIP size, reflecting overwhelming interest from 
high-quality institutional investors. This resounding 
response serves as a strong endorsement of investor 
confidence in our long-term strategy and growth 
trajectory.  
Among the defining milestones we achieved during 
the year, a major highlight was the performance 
of our Mumbai portfolio, which, for the first time, 
surpassed Bengaluru in quarterly sales during Q4 
FY 25. The launch of Prestige Nautilus recorded an 
outstanding ~ ₹ 2,400 Cr in sales within just a month, 
an exceptional accomplishment that highlights the 
strength of our brand, the relevance of our product 
offerings, and the growing trust we are cultivating in 
new strategic markets. Our growing success in new 
geographies reflects our evolution into a truly pan-
India player, with Bengaluru remaining a strong 
foundation for our continued expansion.Further strengthening our credentials, we 
successfully renewed our CRISIL DA1+ Developer 
Grading – an external validation of our governance 
integrity, operational agility, financial prudence 
and execution capabilities. Simultaneously, we 
took a significant step forward in unlocking value in 
our hospitality business. In April 2025, we filed the 
Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) for Prestige 
Hospitality Ventures Limited with SEBI, setting the 
stage for an IPO of the Hospitality Vertical. The 
primary objective of this move is to completely 
deleverage the hospitality vertical, thereby cleaning 
up the debt on its books and creating headroom for 
focussed and sustainable growth in this important 
segment. 
Collectively, these milestones take us beyond our 
operational success, as they mark our transition 
into a curve of targeted scaling, sharper capital 
stewardship, and readiness to lead with greater 
resilience.a strong and well-curated project pipeline for FY 26, 
carrying an estimated Gross Development Value 
(GDV) of around ₹ 42,000 Cr This portfolio, spread 
across key cities including Bengaluru, Mumbai, 
Hyderabad, Chennai, Goa, and the National Capital 
Region (NCR), equips us with the agility, diversity, 
and scale required to respond to shifting market 
dynamics, while sustaining long-term growth.
Even as we scale new heights, we remain 
grounded in our commitment to sustainability and 
inclusive growth, ensuring our developments serve 
communities and the environment.These milestones take us 
beyond our operational 
success, as they mark our 
transition into a curve of 
targeted scaling, sharper 
capital stewardship, and 
readiness to lead with greater 
resilience.
Expanding Horizons with Strong 
Delivery and Pipeline
FY 25 laid the groundwork for a turning point in 
our geographic diversification strategy, setting the 
stage for the successful delivery of our first marquee 
projects in Mumbai, The Prestige Jasdan Classic, 
Siesta at The Prestige City, Mulund, and Prestige 
Turf Tower at Mahalaxmi, which were completed in 
the early part of FY 26. These handovers signalled 
our growing emphasis on westward expansion and 
also reaffirmed our ability to execute landmark 
developments in India’s most competitive real 
estate hubs. Our widening footprint is supported by The Way Forward
As we continue to bolster our presence in key urban 
corridors, our focus remains on capital efficiency, 
design excellence, and consistent delivery – 
ensuring that each project contributes meaningfully 
to our aspiration of delivering customer delight 
through timely execution and high-quality 
developments. Backed by a solid foundation and 
a future-fit pipeline, we are confidently positioned

Our Malls have emerged as cultural

park we develop becomes a catalyst for local employment, ancillary business

activity in both urban and emerging corridors.
Our projects across metros and Tier-2 cities play a pivotal role in expanding civic infrastructure, attracting 
investments, and supporting community upliftment through better housing, connectivity, and quality of life.

empowers individuals, businesses and cities alike.

Grounded in ResponsibilitySustainable Construction Practices

environmental responsibility into the very fabric of our real estate operations.
Why it Matters
Buildings contribute to nearly 40% of global energy-related emissions, with over 90% of these emissions 
generated during their operational life. Reducing this footprint requires a shift in how buildings are designed, 
built, and run.
At Prestige, we approach construction as a long-term climate responsibility. Sustainability is integrated 
from the drawing board to delivery, ensuring our developments are efficient, resilient, and environmentally 
conscious.

Swing, Putt, and Pollinate: How Prestige Golfshire is 
Championing BiodiversityCASE STUDY
At Prestige Group, we are committed to 
ensuring that luxury developments co-
exist with biodiversity, creating spaces that 
nurture both people and the planet. 
Nestled at the foot of Nandi Hills, Prestige 
Golfshire has long been an icon of luxury 
hospitality and world-class golfing. Now, it is 
also home to a thriving apiary, an initiative 
designed to enhance biodiversity, support 
pollination, and integrate responsible 
ecological practices into the fabric of our 
operations. 
In collaboration with a specialised 
beekeeping partner, we set up 50 hive units 
across two key locations - within the golf 
course and its surrounding areas covering 
approximately 300 square meters. Within just four months, the first honey 
harvest yielded an impressive 15 litres - a 
testament to the thriving conditions for our 
bee colonies. The honey, distinct in its deep 
brown colour and rich, earthy flavour, is 
unlike mass-produced varieties, reflecting 
the uniqueness of the surrounding flora. 
Golf courses, often criticised for high 
water usage and manicured landscapes, 
are evolving into biodiversity hubs when 
designed thoughtfully. The Prestige Golfshire 
apiary initiative is a step towards integrating 
nature-positive land management into 
hospitality and recreational spaces, proving 
that luxury and ecological responsibility can 
go hand in hand.

Integrated Water Planning at 
Design Stage
Water efficiency begins at the design phase, 
where projects are aligned to defined 
consumption benchmarks across indoor, 
outdoor, and utility areas. These standards 
are built into commissioning plans to ensure 
functionality from day one.
Smart Monitoring for Performance 
Control
Real-time analytics and smart metering 
are deployed to track water use against 
targets. This system enables precise  
management, early leak detection, and 
continuous optimization.
Fixture and Landscape Efficiency
Projects incorporate dual-flush systems, flow 
restrictors, and leak sensors to reduce internal 
consumption. Outdoor areas use drip irrigation 
and drought-tolerant landscaping to limit non-
essential water use.
Closed-Loop Reuse Systems
Rainwater harvesting infrastructure supports 
reuse across flushing, cooling, and cleaning 
functions. Additionally, STPs process greywater 
and stormwater, ensuring efficient recycling for 
non-potable needs.

Shaping Tomorrow’s Urban Living, TodayCASE STUDY
Most cities grow by adding more concrete, 
more traffic, and more distance between 
people and nature. But The Prestige City 
Indirapuram imagines something different: a 
neighbourhood where every design choice 
reclaims what urban life has lost – the fresh 
air, green spaces, and genuine connection.
Imagine waking up to the sound of trees 
stirring in the breeze, to stepping outside 
your door and walking along car-free 
boulevards lined with flowering gardens and 
shaded skywalks. Over 25 acres of green 
landscapes are not just decorative, they are 
the heart of daily life. From meditation lawns 
and reflexology paths to tree houses and 
edible gardens, every space invites you to 
slow down, breathe deeper, and reconnect 
with the rhythms of nature. Instead of 
exhaust fumes and honking horns, there are 
quiet places to pause, chat, and gather .
Inside each home, natural light floods 
through large sliding windows, thoughtfully 
placed so that more than 75% of living areas 
feel bright and open. Deep overhangs shade 
interiors from glare and heat, creating a 
cool retreat without shutting out daylight. 
In addition, more than 30% of car parking 
spaces are equipped with EV charging 
points. 
Sustainability here is an infrastructure you 
can feel. Walls and roofs are insulated to keep heat out and comfort in. LED lighting 
cuts energy use by up to 30%. High-
efficiency, HCFC-free air conditioning cools 
responsibly. A 100-kW solar PV system 
offsets emissions every day. These measures 
combine to achieve a 14.5% reduction in 
total energy consumption, helping families 
lower their environmental footprint without 
giving up modern comforts.
Water conservation is visible in every corner . 
Low-flow fixtures reduce daily water use by 
over 41%. Each rainfall captures more than  
1.1 million of rainwater, enough to meet  
nearly a full day’s water needs for all 
residents. Combined with in-house 
sewage treatment and smart irrigation, 
these systems save the equivalent of over 
32,000 tanker trips each year, preventing 
an estimated 1,722 metric tonnes of CO2 
emissions by keeping diesel trucks off the 
road.
With its launch planned for FY 26, The 
Prestige City Indirapuram is set to go beyond 
living spaces, shaping a vibrant way of life. 
It is a place to become. To choose days 
filled with more sunlight, more greenery, 
more connection, and more purpose. It is an 
invitation to a world of infinite possibilities, 
where every detail, from the paint on the 
walls to the water in your glass, is part of a 
shared commitment to a better future.

Embedding a Safety-First CultureCASE STUDY
With large-scale developments across 
residential, commercial, and retail 
segments, Prestige Group recognised 
the need to elevate occupational health 
and safety (OHS) standards. Fragmented 
practices and growing site complexities 
demanded a structured, organization-
wide transformation to ensure zero-harm 
workplaces.
Strategic Response
Prestige launched a formal journey to 
embed a world-class Occupational 
Health and Safety Management System 
(OHSM S) across all sites, anchored in the  
British Safety Council’s (BSC) Five-
Star Framework.  This brought global 
benchmarks, leadership ownership, and 
cultural integration to the forefront of its 
safety approach.
Key interventions included:
  Seven pilot projects  chosen across asset 
classes to test and standardise safety 
systems
  OHS leadership training  for senior 
management to drive top-down 
accountability
  Centralised MIS platform  for real-time 
safety data, audits, and benchmarking
  Mandatory safety induction  rolled out 
for all site entrants, including employees, 
contractors, vendors, and visitors  Structured training  for over 600  
personnel , covering technical, 
behavioural, and emergency response 
modules
Impact
The transformation delivered measurable 
improvements in safety awareness, 
reporting discipline, and risk mitigation. 
Standardization across project lifecycles 
helped embed safety into everyday 
decision-making, while leadership visibility  
reinforced a culture of collective  
responsibility.
  Safety protocols now operational across 
pilot and non-pilot sites
  MIS-driven data visibility enables 
proactive risk management
  Workforce competency significantly 
enhanced through role-based training
  Safety committees and stakeholder 
engagement mechanisms 
institutionalised
By aligning global best practices with 
local execution, the Group has redefined 
workplace safety across its projects. 
The initiative showcases how structured 
systems, empowered teams, and leadership 
commitment can collectively create safer, 
more resilient built environments.

Sustainable Supply Chain 
ManagementSocial: Supply Chain Management
Environment Social Governance
Our commitment to inclusive and responsible growth also extends to our 
suppliers and contractors – critical stakeholders in translating our ESG vision 
into on-ground impact. In real estate, the sustainability of outcomes depends 
on how responsibly materials, services, and execution partners are sourced and 
managed. Our supply chain practices focus on traceability, ESG compliance, 
and minimising environmental impact across projects.
Sustainable supply chain management is integral 
to ensuring ethical sourcing, operational resilience, 
and long-term value creation in real estate. 
Our approach will focus on further aligning suppliers 
and contractors with clearly defined ESG standards 
right from the procurement stage. We aim to embed 
responsible practices early in the process, ensuring 
that sustainability remains a priority throughout 
the value chain. We will enhance our structured 
assessments, compliance checks, and continuous 
monitoring to strengthen accountability among our 
partners. By advancing our sustainability integration 
into supplier onboarding, reporting, and evaluation, 
we expect to promote greater transparency, 
mitigate risks, and facilitate environmentally 
responsible project execution.
Key initiatives include:
  Conducting comprehensive ESG assessments as 
a standard practice.
  Implementing robust compliance and ESG 
integration processes for all suppliers and 
contractors.
  Establishing a grievance redressal mechanism to 
ensure open communication and support for our 
suppliers and contractors.Through these initiatives, we aim to strengthen the 
transparency, resilience, and responsibility of our 
supply chain – ensuring it supports both operational 
excellence and our broader ESG goals. By fostering 
ethical and collaborative partnerships, we enhance 
our capacity to deliver sustainable developments, 
reinforce stakeholder confidence, and create long-
term value across the real estate ecosystem.

A Workplace that Cares – Wellness Beyond the DeskCASE STUDY
Most office buildings are designed to house 
people. At Prestige, we design them to uplift 
people. We believe that true workplace 
wellness is not just about having a gym 
or a quiet room, it is about creating an 
environment where individuals feel cared 
for, included, and connected.
This belief has shaped our approach to 
commercial campuses, where wellness 
is not treated as a perk, but as a shared 
purpose. Over the past year, we have 
transformed our spaces into ecosystems 
that support holistic well-being and 
inclusive programming that puts people 
first.
One standout example is our Cervical 
Cancer Awareness Campaign, held in 
partnership with Apollo Hospitals. The 
initiative reached nearly 950 individuals 
across three major campuses, offering over 
180 women the opportunity to undergo 
screenings right at the workplace. For 
many, it was their first screening. 
Another milestone was our Free Diabetic 
Health Camp, conducted in collaboration 
with Dr . Mohan’s Specialities Centre. Over 
1,200 individuals, including employees, 
support staff, and campus vendors, benefited from free screening, diagnosis, 
and lifestyle guidance. For some, it was a first 
step toward better health after years without 
medical attention.
Wellness at Prestige is also about creating 
moments of joy and connection. From serene 
candle bar socials to impromptu flash mobs, 
we bring people together in ways that lighten 
the workday and deepen interpersonal bonds. 
These experiences help make our campuses 
not just places to work, but places where 
people feel at home.
Inclusivity is another pillar of our wellness 
journey. During Pride Month 2024, more than 
6,000 people across 12 campuses participated 
in vibrant celebrations, featuring drag queen 
performances, selfie booths, and allyship 
workshops.  
Looking ahead, we are investing in AI-enabled 
behavioural wellness tools and forging deeper 
community health partnerships. Our goal is to 
make preventive care, emotional well-being, 
and inclusive culture seamlessly accessible 
within the workplace ecosystem.
At Prestige, we build spaces where people are 
seen, supported, and empowered to live well, 
every day.

Building Safer and Stronger CommunitiesCASE STUDY
At Prestige Group, our commitment to 
community development and operational 
excellence is reflected through the efforts of 
our property management team. This year, 
CSR and safety initiatives demonstrated how 
small, sustained actions can create a lasting 
impact. 
On World Environment Day, we have led the 
beautification of the Government Museum 
on Kasturba Road in partnership with The 
Ugly Indian. What began as a beautification 
drive evolved into a celebration of heritage, 
bringing together over 50 volunteers to 
revive a key cultural landmark. This event 
underscored the power of civic engagement 
and environmental stewardship. 
Addressing the rising public safety concerns, 
we installed solar-powered CCTV cameras 
across vulnerable zones, which is an 
innovative step combining renewable energy 
with community protection. As part of the 
National Road Safety Month, we reached over 
one lakh commuters across six key junctions 
in Bengaluru. With the support of traffic 
police and wardens, our team promoted road 
safety awareness, pedestrian rights, and responsible driving, making it one of our most 
visible community-facing campaigns to date. 
Internally, we embedded safety deeply into 
our operating culture. Through the Emergency 
Response Team (ERT), we trained over 100 staff 
with critical emergency preparedness skills 
across residential and commercial properties. 
At Prestige Technostar, Hazard Identification 
and Risk Assessment (HIRA) sessions 
empowered teams to spot and mitigate 
risks early. Large-scale mock drills, involving 
over 2,000 participants, tested response  
systems and strengthened confidence in real-
life emergency scenarios. Our STP training 
sessions focussed on efficient wastewater 
treatment operations and safety practices, 
training over 200 staff across multiple locations. 
Daily Toolbox Talks also played a key role in 
building a safety-first mindset among our site 
teams, reinforcing practical lessons on PPE, 
electrical safety, fall prevention, and real-time 
incident response. 
Through these initiatives, we continue to 
uphold the values of care, accountability, and 
preparedness, ensuring that the communities 
we manage are well-maintained, empowered, 
safe, and future-ready.
By maintaining active engagement with our customers post-possession, we reinforce trust and long-term 
relationships. Our integrated approach not only safeguards the quality of delivered assets but also generates 
recurring value and enhances stakeholder satisfaction across the lifecycle of our developments.annuity-based business spans facility management, 
housekeeping, security, leasing, fit-outs, and post-
possession services. As of FY 25, we managed 181 
projects covering 110 Sq. Ft. across residential, 
commercial, and retail developments.

The Wisdom that  
Shapes Our Direction.Board of Directors and Leadership Team
About Our Board
At Prestige, our Board of Directors carries the 
collective responsibility of steering our Company 
with persistent focus and clarity. They set the tone 
for ethical governance and ensure the organization 
stands as a responsible corporate citizen. Serving 
as the vital bridge between stakeholders and our 
Company, the Board champions transparency and 
open communication at every turn. 
In alignment with the Companies Act and SEBI 
Listing Regulations, a formal and thoughtful 
evaluation process measures the effectiveness of 
the Board, its committees and individual members, 
including the Chairperson. This assessment, guided 
by a structured questionnaire, explores every 
dimension of the Board’s performance. 
Comprising 4 executive directors and 4 independent 
directors, this diverse 8-member group brings a 
wealth of expertise that continuously strengthens 
our governance framework. To effectively supervise 
vital business operations, we have implemented 
a range of committees. Our leadership team is 
responsible for supervising the ESG aspects, which 
undergo regular evaluations by our Board. 
Under the purview of decision-making and 
oversight roles, our Board holds responsibilities 
including but not limited to:
  Monitoring legislative, regulatory, and 
governance compliance
  Ensuring effective remuneration policies and 
practices
  Developing a framework for delegating authority 
to Executive Directors and lines of management
  Adopting our strategy and budget based on 
management proposals
  Navigating the economic landscape to help 
achieve set targets, execute plans, and monitor 
performance
  Making decisions on financing transactions and 
overseeing equity management
  Ensuring implementation of policies and ethical 
conduct in all operations  Overseeing transformation, diversity, 
empowerment, and a culture of inclusivity
  Ensuring effective, risk-based internal audits and 
monitoring the effectiveness of internal controls
The Board Committees hold a crucial position 
within Prestige’s governance structure and are 
formed to address specific areas or activities that 
are of concern to our Company and require closer 
examination. These Committees are officially 
approved by the Board and are responsible for 
carrying out well-defined roles that are typically 
performed by Board members as a part of good 
governance practices. The Board oversees the 
Committees’ performance of their duties and is 
accountable for their actions. The Chairman of each 
Committee provides the Board with a summary 
of the discussions conducted during Committee 
Meetings. Currently, the Board has established the 
following Committees, both statutory and non-
statutory.
  Audit Committee 
  Nomination and Remuneration Committee 
  Stakeholders’ Relationship Committee 
  Management Sub-Committee 
  Corporate Social Responsibility Committee 
  Risk Management Committee

  ESG Committee

Irfan Razack is a prominent figure in the real estate 
sector, recognised for his visionary leadership 
and significant contributions as the Chairman 
of Prestige Group. With over several decades 
of experience, Razack has played a crucial role 
in developing Prestige Group into one of India’s 
top real estate companies. His commitment to 
excellence, steadfast resolve, and strategic insight 
have established the Company as a pioneer in the 
field.
Born and raised in Bengaluru, India, Irfan Razack 
hails from a family with a deep-rooted legacy in 
the construction business. His father, Razack Sattar, 
laid the foundation of Prestige Group in 1986, and 
Irfan joined the Company shortly after its inception. 
He started his journey by working alongside his 
brothers, Rezwan and Noaman, under the guidance 
of his father, learning the intricacies of the trade and 
gaining valuable industry insights.
Under Irfan Razack’s astute leadership, Prestige 
Group has witnessed unparalleled growth and 
expansion. The Company has emerged as a 
prominent player in the real estate market, known 
for its iconic residential, commercial, retail, and 
hospitality projects. With a focus on quality, 
innovation, and customer-centricity, Razack 
has steered Prestige Group towards numerous 
achievements and accolades.
Razack’s visionary approach has been instrumental 
in identifying and capitalising on emerging 
opportunities within the real estate industry. He 
has steered the Company through various market 
fluctuations, effectively overcoming challenges and 
reliably achieving excellent outcomes. His acute 
comprehension of market trends, combined with his 
capacity to anticipate the changing requirements 
of clients, has allowed Prestige Group to maintain a 
competitive edge.
Beyond his contributions to the real estate 
industry, Irfan Razack is known for his philanthropic endeavours. He believes in giving back to society 
and actively engages in various initiatives 
focused on education, healthcare, and community 
welfare. As a responsible corporate citizen, he 
has initiated several sustainable practices within 
the organization, emphasising environmental 
conservation and social responsibility.
Razack’s leadership style is characterised by 
his hands-on approach, accessible demeanour, 
and commitment to fostering a positive work 
culture. He places great importance on building 
strong relationships with stakeholders, including 
employees, customers, and partners. His ability to 
inspire and motivate teams has been instrumental 
in nurturing a talented workforce dedicated to 
delivering excellence in every aspect of Prestige 
Group’s operation.
Under Razack’s leadership, Prestige Group has 
received numerous awards and recognitions, both 
nationally and internationally. The Company’s 
dedication to quality, innovation, and customer 
satisfaction has been acknowledged by respected 
industry bodies and publications, further 
strengthening its reputation as a prominent real 
estate developer .
Considered one of the leading authorities on real

Professional and Personal Profile
As the Co-Founder of Prestige Estates Projects 
Ltd., Rezwan Razack brings in over four decades 
of experience into the business of property 
development. Rezwan Razack is the Managing 
Director of Prestige Group, India’s leading property 
developer, where he has played a pivotal role in 
taking the Company to its present level. 
The second son of Razack Sattar, Rezwan entered 
his family’s retail business in 1975 and diversified 
into property development in 1985. Rezwan has 
inherited his father’s zest for excellence and has 
been an achiever . 
Rezwan Razack’s pleasant demeanour and affable 
nature has been an asset for the Group’s team 
building efforts. He mainly handles all construction 
and engineering works at Prestige Group, where 
he has built a highly motivated team. His excellent 
people skills have created an environment where 
team members can execute assignments with 
confidence and effectiveness. 
Rezwan Razack is also responsible for having 
completed 305 developments of the Prestige Group 
pan India both residential and commercial including 
plots, apartments, villas, townhouses, IT parks, leisure, 
retail and hospitality totalling to 190 Mn Sq. Ft.
Philanthropic Works
Rezwan Razack is a visionary whose contributions 
extend far beyond the realm of business. A dedicated 
philanthropist, he played a pivotal role in organising 
the ‘Terry Fox Run’ in Bengaluru - a fundraising event 
in support of cancer research. In recognition of his 
efforts, Rezwan was honoured with a Medallion and 
Scroll by the Governor General of Canada, Mr . David 
Johnston, during his State visit in 2014. 
Dr . Rezwan Razack
Joint Managing Director
Rezwan is also a steadfast supporter of the PRAY

Rezwan Razack is actively involved in various

Academy for Skill Training, and the Public Arts Trust 
of India, a non-profit organization. 
Rezwan’s multifaceted interests highlight his

photographer, he also follows Formula 1 motorsports 
with great enthusiasm and is an innovative cook. 
His hobbies and passions have been shaped by his 
extensive travels across the globe. 
Numismatics 
Rezwan Razack started collecting Indian Paper 
Money as his childhood hobby. Over the past nearly 
60 years, Rezwan has accomplished a specialised 
collection comprising one note of each variety of 
Paper Money pertaining to India since inception to 
the present. This is today the most comprehensive 
collection in the world and displayed at the renowned 
‘Rezwan Razack’s Museum of Indian Paper Money’ 
situated in Bengaluru, India. 
‘The Revised Standard Reference Guide to Indian 
Paper Money’, a book that Rezwan Razack co-
authored and released in January 2012, is currently 
the single most reliable point of reference on Indian 
Paper Money globally. 
In 2017, Rezwan Razack authored the book ‘One 
Rupee - One Hundred Years 1917-2017’ to mark the 
One Hundredth Anniversary of the issue of the One 
Rupee note in India.

IBNS India Banknote Collectors’ Chapter
Rezwan Razack structured the formation of the India 
Chapter of the International Bank Note Society in 
2010 and is currently the Chairman of ‘IBNS – India 
Banknote Collectors’ Chapter’. 
Rezwan regularly conducts IBNS IBCC Meetings 
every quarter for Indian Paper Money enthusiasts. 
Rezwan shares his knowledge with students to 
promote numismatics as a hobby. He organises 
numismatic events, seminars, competitions and is 
highly approachable t o the numismatic fraternity. He 
encourages budding collectors and writes regularly 
on Indian Paper Money for numismatic publications 
in India and overseas.

ECONOMIC OVERVIEW
India’s economy grew at a robust 6.5% in FY 25, 
sustaining its momentum despite continued global 
economic volatility. This steady performance 
underscores the strength of India’s domestic 
economic framework and the effectiveness of its 
carefully calibrated policy measures in addressing 
challenges like trade disruptions and tariff 
uncertainties.
A major contributor to this resilience is robust 
domestic consumption, with rural demand serving 
as a crucial buffer against external shocks. This 
internal stability, along with ongoing structural 
reforms, rapid digital adoption, and sustained 
infrastructure investments, continues to strengthen 
India’s macroeconomic foundation.A major driver of India’s economic transformation 
is the Union Budget for FY 26, which introduced 
progressive tax reforms aimed at boosting 
disposable incomes, especially for the middle class 
and salaried individuals. One of the key proposals 
includes raising the basic income tax exemption 
limit to ₹ 4 Lakhs and a complete waiver of tax 
liability for individuals earning up to ₹ 12 Lakhs 
annually under the new tax regime. These measures 
are expected to result in meaningful tax savings, 
thereby enhancing household spending capacity. 
While the immediate fiscal relief is clear, the broader 
impact on consumption trends, saving behaviour, 
and demand for premium products is anticipated 
to materialise progressively as these reforms are 
implemented.
(Source:https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.
aspx?PRID=2098406)
In parallel, the Government of India has reaffirmed its 
commitment to infrastructure-led growth. The Union 
Budget 2025-26 allocates ₹ 11.21 Lakh Cr towards 
capital expenditure, marginally higher than the  
₹ 11.11 Lakh Cr allocated in the previous fiscal year . 
This sustained fiscal thrust is driving development 
across vital sectors such as transportation, energy, 
and urban mobility, with significant investments 
in roads, railways, aviation, and urban transit 
networks.
(Source:https://www.ey.com/en_in/technical/alerts-hub/2025/02/
budget-2025-infrastructure-sector)
Additionally, India’s services sector continues to play 
a pivotal role in sustaining the country’s economic 
momentum, with projected growth of 7.2% in FY 25. 
This strong performance is underpinned by robust 
activity across financial services, healthcare, 
hospitality, and public administration. A recovery in 
consumer spending, alongside a marked increase in 
domestic tourism, has further driven demand across 
these key segments.India is well-positioned to sustain a robust real 
GDP growth rate of 6.5% between FY 26 and FY 28, 
reinforcing its status as one of the fastest-growing 
major economies globally. This growth trajectory 
is underpinned by a diverse set of drivers. Rising 
private consumption, particularly in rural regions, 
is being buoyed by an expanding middle class 
and steady increases in per capita income. At 
the same time, momentum in manufacturing 
and infrastructure continues to build, supported 
by flagship initiatives such as ‘Make in India’ and 
the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes, 
as well as substantial capital infusion in transport, 
logistics, and digital infrastructure.
However, external headwinds remain a concern. 
A potential slowdown in key global markets, 
including the United States and China, could 
impact export-linked sectors. Even so, India’s 
growth outlook remains firmly anchored in strong 
macroeconomic fundamentals and proactive 
policy frameworks. Sustained monitoring of 
global developments will be crucial to navigating 
uncertainties and ensuring continued economic 
resilience.
(Source:https://www.ubs.com/global/en/investment-bank/
insights-and-data/2024/indias-outlook-2025-2026-story.html)GDP Growth in the Last Five

INDIAN REAL ESTATE SECTOR
India’s real estate sector has emerged as a pivotal 
force in driving socioeconomic transformation 
in the world’s largest democracy and second-
most populous nation. Once largely informal and 
fragmented, the industry has since undergone a 
significant evolution.
Urban migration, rising demand for residential and 
commercial spaces, and the expansion of industrial 
corridors and city boundaries have been central 
to this growth story. These trends, combined with 
the rapid pace of economic development, have 
propelled real estate into one of the country’s most 
dynamic and influential sectors.
Over time, strategic government interventions have 
played a vital role in shaping the industry - through the 
introduction of sector-specific regulations, reforms 
to streamline governance, and initiatives aimed at 
improving transparency and investor confidence. In 
FY 25, the sector stands at the confluence of policy, 
population growth, and economic ambition, poised 
to play an even greater role in India’s development 
journey.
Decarbonization and digital transformation are set 
to be the two most transformative forces reshaping 
the real estate sector over the coming decade. The industry is steadily embracing sustainable 
development practices, integrating green building 
principles and climate-conscious design into core 
project strategies. Green real estate is no longer 
an exception but is becoming the standard, as 
developers align their operations with global 
sustainability benchmarks to reduce emissions and 
meet long-term environmental targets.
At the same time, technology adoption is redefining 
operational efficiency. The rise of PropTech is 
transitioning from experimentation to mainstream 
adoption, as firms deploy digital tools to streamline 
operations, enhance transparency, and improve 
asset performance. Emerging technologies such as 
the Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence, 
and Big Data are being used for everything from 
real-time monitoring and predictive maintenance 
to smarter decision-making. Together, these 
innovations are helping the sector build a more 
resilient, efficient, and future-ready real estate 
ecosystem.
(Source:https://www.cbre.co.in/insights/articles/mapping-the-
evolution-of-indian-real-estate-a-glimpse-into-the-75-year-
journey)
Government Initiatives
The Union Budget for FY 26 unveiled a series of progressive policy interventions aimed at catalysing growth in 
India’s real estate sector . With a clear emphasis on affordable housing, infrastructure expansion, and regulatory 
clarity, the budget reflects a strategic alignment between fiscal policy and the sector’s evolving needs. 
SWAMIH Fund 2.0: Expediting Stalled 
Housing Projects
The Indian Government has launched SWAMIH Fund 
2.0, a ₹ 15,000 Cr blended finance vehicle backed 
by the Centre, financial institutions, and private 
investors, aimed at expediting the completion of 
stalled affordable and mid-income housing projects. 
This initiative builds on the success of the original 
SWAMIH scheme, which facilitated the delivery of 
40,000 housing units, and reaffirms the government’s 
continued commitment to supporting affordable 
housing. SWAMIH 2.0 is expected to enable the 
completion of an additional 1 Lakh homes, thereby 
restoring buyer confidence, unlocking capital tied 
up in delayed projects, and injecting vital liquidity 
into the residential real estate segment.
Prestige Nautilus, Mumbai (Artist’s impression) Urban Challenge Fund:  
Catalysing Urban Infrastructure
The Indian Government has introduced a ₹ 1 Lakh Cr 
Urban Challenge Fund to catalyse next-generation 
urban development, with ₹ 10,000 Cr allocated 
for FY 26. This initiative aims to accelerate the 
transformation of urban spaces through targeted 
interventions in critical areas. Key priorities include 
resolving land and infrastructure constraints, 
strengthening social infrastructure, and scaling up 
smart cities and integrated urban transit corridors. 
The Fund will provide up to 25% of project costs, with 
the balance expected to be mobilised through bonds, 
bank financing, and public-private partnership 
(PPP) models.Tax Reforms:  
Boosting Affordability and Compliance
The Union Budget FY 26 introduces key tax reforms 
aimed at enhancing affordability and investor 
confidence in the real estate sector . The TDS 
threshold on rental income has been increased 
from ₹ 2.4 Lakh to ₹ 6 Lakh annually, significantly 
reducing the compliance burden for landlords and 
making rental housing a more attractive asset class 
for investors. 
In addition, income tax rationalization measures, 
particularly the increase in the zero-tax slab to  
₹ 12 Lakh, are expected to boost disposable income, 
especially for the middle-income segment. This 
enhanced purchasing power is likely to stimulate 
housing demand, particularly in the mid-income 
residential category, thereby supporting broader 
sectoral growth.
Infrastructure & State-Level Support: 
Incentivising CAPEX and Accelerating 
Development Initiatives
To drive infrastructure-led growth and urban 
transformation, the government has proposed a  
₹ 1.5 Lakh Cr outlay in the form of interest-free 
50-year loans to states, aimed at incentivising 
capital expenditure and accelerating development 
initiatives. In tandem, key infrastructure ministries

INDIAN RESIDENTIAL SECTOR
India’s residential real estate sector remained 
resilient and vibrant in FY 25, building on strong 
consumer sentiment and structural demand. Housing 
sales touched approximately 4.59 Lakh units in 2024, 
marking an impressive 76% growth over 2019 levels, 
despite a slight 4% moderation from the record pace 
of 2023. This performance was led by major urban 
centres MMR, Pune, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and 
Delhi-NCR, which together accounted for 92% of 
total sales across the top seven cities.
The sustained momentum was driven by rising 
homeownership aspirations, improving income 
levels, and continued progress in infrastructure 
development. Even as the market shows signs of 
consolidation, buyer confidence remains strong, 
with preferences leaning towards well-connected 
locations, reputable developers, and ready or near-
ready inventory. These factors, along with a stable 
interest rate environment and urbanization trends, 
are expected to support steady growth through 
2025.On the supply side, new launches in 2024 stood at 
approximately 4.12 Lakh units, a 7% dip from 2023, 
but a substantial 74% increase over 2019. MMR, 
Hyderabad, Pune, and Bengaluru emerged as the 
key contributors, together accounting for 79% of the 
total new supply. The residential sector appears to 
sustain its upward trajectory, with balanced growth 
anchored in end-user demand and quality-driven 
development.
(Source:https://www.cbre.co.in/insights/articles/mapping-the-
evolution-of-indian-real-estate-a-glimpse-into-the-75-year-
journey)
Policy support such as PMAY-U and the SWAMIH 
Fund has helped unlock stalled supply, while the 
repo rate reduction to 5.50% in June 2025 brought 
effective home loan rates below 8%, thereby 
enhancing affordability. Additionally, developers are 
capitalising on suburban demand through township 
models that integrate apartment complexes with 
plotted villas, signalling a shift towards scale and 
integrated living.

City-Wise Residential Supply Demand Dynamics (CY 24) 
Outlook
India’s residential real estate sector is expected to maintain a strong growth trajectory, underpinned by 
solid market fundamentals. Both sales volumes and new property launches are expected to remain resilient, 
despite potential macroeconomic or policy-related headwinds. While pricing trends may vary across regions 
and asset classes, the premium and luxury residential segments, particularly properties priced at ₹ 2 Cr and 
above, are anticipated to perform well. This sustained demand is being driven by discerning homebuyers who 
increasingly prioritise spacious living environments with seamless access to essential infrastructure and urban 
conveniences.Outlook
India’s commercial real estate sector is well placed 
for sustained growth, underpinned by strong 
macroeconomic fundamentals, rapid urbanization, 
and rising foreign direct investment.  
The increasing role of Real Estate Investment Trusts 
(REITs) and institutional capital is infusing the market 
with greater transparency, liquidity, and investor 
confidence, with more REIT listings anticipated 
in the near future. However, the sector continues 
to grapple with structural challenges such as land 
acquisition hurdles, regulatory complexities, and 
rising construction costs.
Despite these headwinds, the overall outlook 
remains positive. Continued economic expansion, 
evolving workplace models, and supportive 
government initiatives are expected to reinforce 
India’s position as a key destination for commercial 
real estate investment.INDIAN COMMERCIAL SECTOR
India’s commercial real estate sector witnessed a 
landmark year in 2024, driven by strong occupier 
confidence, expansion by global and domestic firms, 
and a wave of new entrants. The market is projected 
to expand from US$ 49.30 Bn in FY 25 to US$ 128.40 
Bn by FY 30, clocking in a strong CAGR of 21.1%. This 
momentum is being driven by a combination of 
economic expansion, improved transparency, robust 
FDI inflows, and supportive government initiatives 
such as Smart City and AMRUT that are boosting 
infrastructure development.
The Indian office sector is witnessing a paradigm 
shift, driven by the rise of flexible workspaces 
that are transforming how businesses operate. 
This transformation is being propelled by robust 
leasing activity, as companies increasingly prioritise 
adaptability, cost-efficiency, and employee-centric 
environments. The growing demand for hybrid 
work models has accelerated the adoption of 
flexible office formats, positioning them as a core 
component of corporate real estate strategies. As 
a result, traditional leasing patterns are evolving to 
accommodate dynamic workforce needs and shorter-
term commitments, reflecting a broader shift towards 
agility and operational resilience in the commercial 
real estate landscape. Office space absorption grew 
by 17% year-on-year to reach 79 Mn Sq. Ft. in 2024, 
underscoring sustained demand amid evolving 
talent and technology ecosystems. Key markets like 
Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, and Delhi-NCR led 
this activity, collectively accounting for 74% of total 
office space absorbed.
On the supply side, development completions reached 
52.3 Mn Sq. Ft., showcasing the sector’s continued 
resilience. The new supply was defined by superior, 
amenity-rich, and experiential assets, with a growing 
preference for larger floor plates and green-certified 
buildings, which made up 65% of total new stock. 
Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, and Pune were 
at the forefront of new supply additions, together 
contributing ~79% of all completions.
With absorption outpacing supply in many markets, 
vacancy levels declined, and rents rose in select micro-
markets, indicating tightening market conditions. 
Overall, India’s office segment remained robust, 
supported by strong fundamentals and increasing 
investor and occupier interest in sustainable, well-
designed workspaces.
(Source:CBRE Research Report, March 2025)

INDIAN RETAIL SECTOR
India’s retail sector is undergoing a remarkable 
transformation, driven by a confluence of powerful 
macroeconomic forces. Accelerated urbanization, 
rising disposable incomes, and the evolving 
aspirations of the burgeoning middle class have 
collectively created fertile ground for vibrant leasing 
activity across the country. These shifts in consumer 
behaviour and preferences are reshaping the retail 
landscape, fuelling robust demand for physical retail 
spaces. 
The strong leasing momentum seen over the past 
two years has carried forward into 2024, reflecting 
sustained demand across India’s major cities. 
Retail leasing activity in India’s Tier-I cities reached 
approximately 6.4 Mn Sq. Ft. in 2024. Homegrown 
retailers were at the forefront of this growth, 
particularly in segments such as mid-range fashion, 
jewellery, casual dining, chef-led restaurants, and 
entertainment. The surge in leasing was primarily 
fuelled by demand for second-generation spaces 
across various retail formats, even as new supply 
remained limited, with just 1.2 Mn Sq. Ft. added across 
cities like Hyderabad, Bengaluru, and Mumbai during 
the year .
Another significant development in recent years 
has been the rapid expansion of direct-to-consumer 
(D2C) brands. As digital-first businesses seek to 
establish a physical presence, demand for flexible, 
omnichannel retail spaces has grown. These formats 
enable seamless integration between online and 
offline strategies, improving customer outreach and 
brand visibility. At the same time, sustained demand 
for premium products, supported by higher disposable 
incomes, has driven the growth of luxury retail. Retail Supply-Absorption Trends 
(2021-24) (in Mn Sq. Ft.)

growth driver for retail real estate, leveraging 
the ‘Made in India’ narrative, improved inventory 
management, and digital sales channels such as 
social media and quick commerce. Their increasing 
focus on personalization and physical touchpoints 
highlights a broader trend of convergence between 
e-commerce and brick-and-mortar retail.
Outlook
Retail demand in India, particularly for primary 
leasing, is projected to strengthen, supported by a 
robust supply pipeline that’s expected to surpass 
past levels. Several new developments across 
key Tier-I cities are poised for completion, further 
boosting momentum in the sector .
Domestic direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands are 
likely to drive a significant share of this demand, 
with a continued shift towards physical retail to 
deepen customer engagement and personalise 
experiences. As India’s D2C market expands, brands 
are focussing on enhancing reach and conversion 
through social media, quick commerce, smarter 
inventory strategies, and higher repeat purchase 
rates.
(Source:CBRE Report)
Outlook
India’s hospitality sector is on a strong growth 
trajectory, building on the sustained momentum of 
the past two years. This upward trend is underpinned 
by a robust domestic tourism market, the emergence 
of niche travel segments, a gradual revival in 
inbound tourism, and continued infrastructure 
development. As domestic travel continues to 
gain traction, rising discretionary spending and 
evolving traveller preferences are set to further 
catalyse sectoral expansion, reinforcing India’s 
position as a key player in the global hospitality 
landscape. Complementing this growth are ongoing 
infrastructure upgrades and targeted investments 
in high-potential tourist destinations, which are 
expected to significantly elevate the country’s 
tourism and hospitality ecosystem.INDIAN HOSPITALITY SECTOR
In CY 2024, India’s hospitality sector witnessed 
a remarkable resurgence, establishing itself as a 
key driver of economic momentum. The industry 
recorded robust growth in both hotel investments 
and stock market performance, signalling renewed 
confidence among investors. The sector ended 
the year with a nationwide occupancy of 63–65%, 
average room rates (ARR) between ₹ 7,800 and 
₹ 8,000, and revenue per available room (RevPAR) 
ranging from ₹ 5,000 to ₹ 5,200, representing a  
27–29% increase compared to pre-COVID levels. 
Buoyed by this strong performance, hoteliers 
ramped up development activity, leading to a 
record number of hotel brand signings with a 
pronounced focus on Tier-2, Tier-3, and emerging 
leisure destinations.
The sector has been undergoing a remarkable 
transformation, propelled by supportive 
government policies and large-scale infrastructure 
enhancements. Key policy interventions include 
100% FDI through the automatic route and five-
year tax holidays for hotels located near UNESCO 
World Heritage sites. To further streamline 
development, the government set up the Hospitality 
Development and Promotion Board, facilitating 
faster hotel project approvals. Additionally, ₹ 2 Bn 
has been allocated for developing tourist circuits 
across pilgrimage destinations, reinforcing the 
government’s commitment to strengthening 
tourism infrastructure. Collectively, these efforts 
have positioned India among the top 100 global 
destinations for ease of doing business in hospitality.
The industry is also experiencing a significant 
evolution in ownership and operating models. 
Franchise and lease agreements are steadily 
replacing traditional hotel ownership structures. 
Hotel chains are increasingly adopting asset-
light strategies, relying on management contracts 
rather than owning properties to enhance revenue 
efficiency. This shift is particularly prominent in the 
organised hotel segment, driven by a digitally savvy 
consumer base concentrated in urban and high-
income markets. 
Consumer behaviour in the hospitality space 
has seen a marked shift towards experiential 
travel and authentic cultural immersion. This 
evolution is fuelling demand for more localised and 
personalised hospitality experiences. As a result, the tourism sector has become a major contributor 
to employment in India. Staycations have emerged 
as a key trend, prompting leading hotel chains to 
roll out curated packages that cater to this rising 
preference for short, local getaways. Properties 
are also emphasising local cultural integration, 
sustainability, and distinctive experiences to create 
competitive differentiation. This transition has 
catalysed the growth of niche tourism themes such 
as nature-based retreats, heritage tourism, cultural 
excursions, wellness-focussed stays, and the MICE 
(Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions) 
segment. Each of these segments demands tailored 
hospitality solutions and infrastructure to meet 
evolving traveller expectations.
(Source:HVS Anarock India Hospitality Industry Overview 2024)

COMPANY OVERVIEW BUSINESS SEGMENTS
At Prestige, our journey began in 1986 in Bengaluru, 
and over the years, we have grown to become one of 
India’s most respected and accomplished real estate 
developers. With almost four decades of experience 
behind us, we take pride in having delivered 302 
high-quality real estate developments, covering a 
cumulative area of 193 Mn Sq. Ft.
Today, our presence spans 13 major cities across the 
country, a testament to our position as a true pan-
India real estate leader . We operate through a strong 
and agile network of subsidiaries, joint ventures, and 
associates, an integrated structure that allows us to 
maintain consistent execution standards and deliver 
operational excellence across all our projects.
We are known for our design innovation, 
architectural finesse, and continued commitment 
to meeting project timelines, attributes that have 
helped us earn the trust of our customers and 
stakeholders. At the heart of everything we do 
is a customer-first mindset, grounded in quality, 
transparency, and the promise of long-term value. 
This has been the cornerstone of our continued 
growth and the reason we have retained our 
leadership position in the industry.
We are now in the midst of an exciting and 
transformative phase, one that is defined by a 
sharper focus on new markets and a renewed 
commitment to sustainability and innovation. Our 
future-forward approach is built on the belief that development must be inclusive, responsible, and 
environmentally conscious.
To drive our next phase of growth, we are focussed 
on the following key priorities:
 Expanding our land bank and building a robust 
pipeline of launch-ready projects to sustain our 
sales momentum and strengthen our market 
leadership position.
 Maintaining our leadership in established markets 
while strengthening our foothold in recently 
entered geographies to expand our overall 
presence.
 Maintaining discipline in project execution to 
ensure timely delivery and uphold our reputation 
for reliability and consistency.
 Enhancing customer satisfaction across every 
interaction and stage of the customer journey.
 Managing capital prudently while creating long-
term value for all our stakeholders.
 Embedding sustainability into every aspect of our 
development, with a focus on energy efficiency, 
green and safe construction practices, and long-
term environmental impact.
 Leveraging technology and digital tools to 
enhance operational efficiency, improve customer 
experiences, and drive smarter decision-making 
across the value chain.

CAUTIONARY STATEMENTWe have established robust internal control systems that are tailored to the scale, scope, and complexity 
of our operations. This comprehensive framework enables effective oversight of all business processes and 
systems, ensuring consistent quality assurance and reliable operational performance. Our internal controls 
are regularly reviewed and assessed to ensure they remain adequate, effective, and fully compliant with all 
applicable laws and regulations. They are essential to safeguarding our assets and upholding a culture of 
accountability and compliance across the organization. The Audit Committee is responsible for overseeing 
our internal control framework, including the appointment of internal auditors. M/s. Grant Thornton India LLP 
currently serves as our Internal Auditor, providing rigorous, independent evaluations that help strengthen our 
control environment and reinforce our governance practices.
The Group comprises 9,508 permanent employees, supplemented by contractors and subcontractors who enlist 
additional personnel for the Company’s construction and operational projects. Prestige’s workforce stands as 
a pillar of support, guiding the Company through challenging landscapes and emerging stronger . Ensuring 
the welfare of all staff members is of paramount importance, with stringent enforcement of safety protocols 
being a top priority. Prestige places profound value on the dedication and resilience of its team, viewing them 
as the Company’s most invaluable asset. Recognising that an organisation’s vigour, commitment, and pursuit 
of excellence hinge on its employees, Prestige is dedicated to enhancing their skills and capabilities through 
regular learning and development initiatives.

 Prevention of insider trading Policy
  As per the provisions of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider 
Trading) Regulations, 2015, the Company has adopted a 
Code of Conduct to regulate, monitor and report trading 
by designated persons in securities of the Company. 
The policy and procedures are periodically reviewed 
and revised from time to time and communicated to 
the designated persons and is available on the website 
of the Company.
  The Insider Trading Code has been implemented to 
prevent the misuse of unpublished price-sensitive 
information and set a framework, rules, and procedures 
that all concerned parties should follow, both in letter and 
spirit, while trading in listed securities of the Company.
  A digital platform is being maintained by the Company, 
which contains the names and other prescribed 
particulars of the persons covered under the Insider 
Trading Code. This online tracking mechanism helps 
for monitoring trade in the Company’s securities by 
designated persons and taking appropriate action in 
case of any violation/non-compliance of the Company’s 
Insider Trading Code.

20.  CONSERVATION OF ENERGY, TECHNOLOGY 
ABSORPTION AND FOREIGN EXCHANGE  EARNINGS 
AND OUTGO:
  The details of conservation of energy, technology 
absorption, foreign exchange earnings and outgo are 
as follows:
  The Company advances its sustainability agenda by 
integrating energy-efficient practices and adopting 
innovative technologies that enhance performance, 
reduce environmental impact, and deliver long-term 
value. These initiatives align with Green Building 
principles, LEED standards, and the Energy Conservation 
Building Code, ensuring projects meet rigorous 
benchmarks while enhancing occupant well-being.
 a) Conservation of Energy
   We implement measures to cut energy use, 
improve efficiency, and promote sustainable 
design. These span renewable energy, smart 
management, and water-energy efficiency, 
delivering environmental and operational gains.  Key measures include:
  •   Solar-powered landscape lighting and 
increased renewable energy use.
  •   Variable frequency drives (VFDs) and lighting 
timers for energy optimisation.
  •   LEDs, CFLs, energy-efficient signage, and 
daylight sensors to reduce artificial lighting.
  •   High-efficiency HVAC systems exceeding 
ASHRAE 90.1.2010 COP standards, pre-
cooling with heat recovery wheels, and 
demand-controlled ventilation.
  •   Water-saving aerators and STP water 
recycling for gardens, cooling towers, and 
flushing.
  •   High-reflective roofing to reduce heat gain 
and cooling loads.
   These steps lower costs, extend equipment life, 
and create healthier spaces.
 b)  Technology Absorption
   We adopt advanced technologies to boost quality, 
speed processes, and reduce environmental 
impact, ensuring resource efficiency and 
resilience.
  Key measures include:
  •   Low-flow fixtures and fittings reducing 
potable water use by over 50%.
  •   STP-treated water for flushing, landscaping, 
and cooling, with 100% stormwater recharge.
  •   Rainwater harvesting with deep well 
recharge.
  •   Water-cooled chillers and eco-friendly HVAC 
systems with VFDs.
  •   Energy monitoring with individual utility 
meters.
  •   Centralised LPG reticulation to residences.
  •   Reflective window films, transparent ceilings, 
and daylight-optimised design.
  •   EV-ready parking spaces.
  •  Native, drought-tolerant landscaping.
  •  Water-saving housekeeping equipment.
   These innovations enhance environmental 
performance and create cost-efficient, future-
ready spaces.

ANNUAL REPORT ON CSR ACTIVITIES:
1. BRIEF OUTLINE ON CSR POLICY & ACTIVITIES:
  The Board of Directors, upon recommendation of 
the Corporate Social Responsibility Committee, have 
identified the following areas listed in Schedule VII 
of the Companies Act, 2013 for carrying out its CSR 
activities:
	   To pursue shareholder value enhancement and 
societal value creation in a mutually emphasizing 
and synergistic manner through ethical, 
transparent, responsible and human conduct, and 
by staying in compliance with applicable laws.
	   To build cleaner and greener cities and to promote 
sustainability and strive for more efficient and 
effective use of energy and materials.
	   To eradicate hunger, poverty and malnutrition, 
promoting health care including preventive 
health care and sanitation including contribution 
to the Swach Bharat Kosh set-up by the Central 
Government for the promotion of sanitation and 
making available safe drinking water.
	   To promote education, including special education 
among children, women and the differently abled 
and to promote livelihood enhancement projects.
	   To promote gender equality, empowering women, 
setting up homes and hostels for women and 
orphans; setting up old age homes, day care centres and such other facilities for senior citizens 
and measures for reducing inequalities faced by 
socially and economically backward groups.
	   To ensure economic sustainability, ecological 
balance, protection of flora and fauna, animal 
welfare, conservation of natural resources and 
maintaining the quality of soil, air and water.
	   To protect national heritage, art and culture 
including restoration of buildings and sites of 
historical importance and works of art; setting up 
public libraries; promotion and development of 
traditional art and handicrafts.
	   To promote measures for the benefit of armed 
forces veterans, war widows and their dependents.
	   Contribution to the prime minister’s national 
relief fund or any other fund set up by the central 
govt. for socio economic development and relief 
and welfare of the schedule caste, tribes, other 
backward classes, minorities and women.
	   To promote nationally recognised sports and rural 
sports.
	  To Develop Slum Area
	   To promote such other activities towards 
betterment of the society.
	   To manage disaster, including relief, rehabilitation 
and reconstruction activities

The PRESTIGE’s governance philosophy is built on the principles of integrity & transparency, accountability, sustainability 
and fostering stakeholder relationship.
OUR PHILOSOPHY:
Our philosophy revolves around fostering sustainable practices that benefit not only our company but also the communities and 
environments in which we operate. We are committed to nurturing strong and meaningful relationships with our stakeholders 
that is built on trust. Innovation and continuous improvement, coupled with transparent processes, drive our philosophy, 
propelling us to exceed expectations. Customer satisfaction lies at the heart of our philosophy, driving us to consistently deliver 
high-quality products and services that exceed expectations.

Corporate GovernanceCORPORATE GOVERNANCE
Corporate governance at our company involves oversight 
by the Board of Directors and Committees, adherence to 
legal and regulatory frameworks, ethical business policies, 
transparent disclosures, rigorous risk and performance 
management. We prioritize disclosures and transparency, 
fostering accountability across all levels of the organization.
PRESTIGE ADHERES TO GOVERNANCE POLICIES AND 
BENCHMARKS THROUGH THE FOLLOWING PRACTICES:
  Investor Presentation & Investor con calls:  Quarterly 
investor presentations provide updates on operational 
and financial performance, project progress, launches, 
and other relevant details. Additionally, investors are 
engaged through con-calls, ensuring transparency in 
disclosure and operations.
  Quarterly review of internal control:  There is a 
continuous effort at Prestige to review and enhance 
internal controls and risk mitigation strategies, fostering 
adherence to Corporate Governance principles.
  Guidance vs. achievement:  To maintain transparency 
and investor confidence, the Company provides 
guidance on pre-sales at the start of each fiscal year. 
Quarterly evaluations compare actual performance 
against these set targets.
We consider it our inherent responsibility to protect the 
rights of our shareholders and disclose timely, adequate 
and accurate information regarding our financials and performance, as well as the leadership and governance of 
the Company.
CODE OF CONDUCT
Prestige has embraced a robust code of conduct that 
defines the organization’s mission, values and principles, 
linking them with standards of professional conduct. This 
code articulates the values the organization wishes to foster 
in leaders and employees and, in doing so, defines desired 
behaviour. As a result written codes of conduct and ethics 
has become benchmarks against which individual and 
organizational performance is measured.
GOVERNANCE POLICIES:
To preserve the Company’s good corporate governance 
practices and to assure full disclosure, transparency, 
accountability, and stakeholder relationship, Prestige has

 Whistle Blower Policy (Vigil Mechanism)
 Risk Management Policy
 Related Party Transactions Policy
 Corporate Social Responsibility Policy
 Material Subsidiary Policy

 Role of the Board of Directors
  Our Board of directors ensure the company’s prosperity 
by collectively directing the company’s affairs, whilst 
meeting the appropriate interests of its shareholders 
and stakeholders. In addition to business and financial 
issues, Board of Directors deal with challenges and 
issues relating to corporate governance, corporate 
social responsibility and corporate ethics.
  The roles of the Board of Directors inter alia includes 
the following:
 • Establish vision, mission and values
 • Set strategy and structure
 • Leadership and oversight
 • Delegate authority to management
 •  Exercise accountability to shareholders and be 
responsible to relevant stakeholders
 Independent Directors
  Independent Directors are non-executive directors as 
defined under Regulation 16(1)(b) of the SEBI Listing 
Regulations and Section 149(6) of the Act along with 
rules framed thereunder. In terms of Regulation 25(8) of 
SEBI Listing Regulations, they have confirmed that they 
are not aware of any circumstance or situation which 
exists or may be reasonably anticipated that could 
impair or impact their ability to discharge their duties.Corporate Governance (Contd.)
174 Integrated Annual Report  2024-25
 The below parameters are followed by the Company.
  Every Independent Director, at the first meeting of the 
Board in which he/she participates as a Director, and 
thereafter, at the first meeting of the Board in every 
financial year, gives a declaration that he/she meets 
the criteria of independence as provided under the 
Companies Act, 2013 and Listing Regulations. In this 
regard, the Board has obtained declarations from all 
the Independent Directors regarding their eligibility to 
meet the criteria of independence in accordance with 
sub-section 7 of section 149 of the Companies Act, 
2013 & sub-regulation 8 of regulation 25 of the SEBI 
(Listing Obligation & Disclosure) Requirements, 2015. 
Further, the Independent Directors have included their 
names in the data bank of Independent Directors 
maintained with the Indian Institute of Corporate 
Affairs in terms of Section 150 of the Act read with Rule 
6 of the Companies (Appointment and Qualification of
